Job Description

This position assists in the delivery and facilitation of DEQ’s PFAS water programs through project management and coordination, policy development, technical support, and collaboration with programmatic partners. Provides development and implementation of PFAS policies, regulations, guidance, and other technical tools for enhancing the PFAS program’s effectiveness. Provides leadership, direction, and guidance to program staff, and ensures compliance with applicable statutes, policies, commitments, and procedures. Please note this position follows a hybrid work schedule to include both in-office and telework. Candidates must be able to work from the assigned work location in Virginia.

Responsibilities

The primary responsibilities include identifying procedural, policy, guidance, and consistency issues and recommending implementation strategies to enhance program consistency in Central Office and throughout the regional offices. This position ensures that the commitments in the program and the timeframes in procedures and regulations are met.  Produces quarterly, semi-annual, and annual reports on water program activities, as needed.  Coordinates staff review of correspondence, reports, plans, and permits to ensure conformance to and consistent application of procedures, regulations, work plans, sound engineering and ecological practices, and pollution prevention approaches.  Responds to requests for technical and regulatory assistance from staff, regulated community, program partners, consultants, and the public for complex projects and/or enforcement cases.  Provides guidance and training in the technical and regulatory aspects of water programs. Evaluates programs for effectiveness and efficiency and conformance to state/federal laws/regulations and guidelines.

Qualifications

Combination of education or training with major coursework in environmental science or engineering, biological or ecological sciences, hydrology, soil science, aquatic ecology, restoration ecology, hydrology and hydraulics natural resource management or related fields or a combination of education and experience demonstrating an equivalent technical background. 
Demonstrated understanding of the technical and legal requirements of the Clean Water Act, State Water Control Law, and DEQ water program processes such as water permitting, water quality continuous planning, or water supply planning. 
Demonstrated experience in DEQ water program processes is desirable.
Experience with state/public participation guidelines; demonstrated experience in developing, evaluating or implementing procedures and/or guidance. 
Demonstrated knowledge of the Administrative Process Act.
Demonstrated ability to effectively use computer systems and software to include Microsoft Office products.  
Demonstrated knowledge, skills, and abilities in project management and workflow/business process management. 
Demonstrated ability to respond to problems by identifying issues and proposing alternative solutions; seeking to correct the underlying causes of problems rather than the symptoms. 
Strong analytical skills, organizational skills, negotiation skills, facilitation skills, and interpersonal skills. 
Must be able to work independently with minimal supervision, as well as be an integral part of a fast-paced, productive team. 
Must be able to work with multiple stakeholders as necessary to resolve issues while being efficient, transparent, fair and consistent.
Demonstrated experience in effective communication, both orally and in writing, with various levels of stakeholders. 
Demonstrated experience with data analysis, and basic statistics.
This position may require you to operate a state owned or leased vehicle. Therefore, a valid driver's license is required.

About Us

The Virginia Department of Environmental Quality (DEQ) is the primary environmental permitting agency in the Commonwealth of Virginia. It is responsible for administering laws and regulations related to air quality, water quality, water supply, renewable energy, and land protection. Through the dedication and work of over 800 employees across six regional offices and the Central Office in Richmond, DEQ issues permits, conducts monitoring and inspections, and enforces the law.

As part of HDR’s Transportation Business Group, you’ll help shape the systems that move people and goods safely, efficiently, and sustainably. Have a focus on client management and development, serving as a client manager and project manager for future assignments and pursuits with key clients in the area.
Take administrative responsibility for section staff and technical service functions, and lead and coordinate services with other sections.
Be involved in marketing planning, proposals and interviews.
Be directly involved with clients in marketing, project production and related issues.
See that all work is planned, organized, controlled and evaluated through proactive project management system
Implement, monitor and support company policy.
Select, train, develop and manage technical personnel.
Manage and develop multidiscipline teams.
Work cooperatively with marketing staff in local and national marketing and production efforts.
Plan and direct planning and environmental projects.
Prepare, plan and analyze/review technical studies, permit applications, NEPA documents, and similar reports/documents.
Direct work of others in completion of required studies, documents and reports.
Demonstrate extensive public participation, agency coordination, planning and programming experience.
Perform other duties as needed.

Preferred Qualifications

15 years of experience
Master’s degree in environmental science, planning, or related
Experience writing proposals, developing scopes of work, budgets, and schedules for complex environmental projects with multidisciplinary teams and multi-agency efforts, local candidates are preferred
NEPA experience including EIS, EA, and CE, MCDCs, or equivalents
Regulatory permitting experience with 404/401/CAMA/Buffers

A minimum of 10 years experience
Professional registration, license or certification may be required based on role

jobs.description:
Job Description

Posting expires: November 20, 2026

Salary: $58,977 - $86,675

General Description And Classification Standards

Performs supervisory assignments associated with operating the water/wastewater treatment plant and to ensure a continuous, adequate supply of potable drinking water meeting federal/state regulations for the citizens of Atlanta. Supervises; water analysis and treatment; mixing chemicals; laboratory testing; operating various pumps and valves; repairing and maintaining machinery and equipment; maintaining records, instructing and disciplining assigned staff. This is a team lead or "foreman" level position with a formally designated team of skilled employees, either in one or multiple skilled specialties. Lead assignments made on a job-by-job basis would be more appropriately at the Senior level. Supervision Received Direction received is very general and focuses on end results and is typically collaborative in nature. Makes decisions on technical issues, diagnoses, or procedures in collaboration with supervisors or managers.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

These are typical responsibilities for this position and should not be construed as exclusive or all inclusive. May perform other duties as assigned. Generates work orders in maintenance management system; orders chemicals and supplies. Coordinates with contractors on plant upgrades and equipment repairs and installations. Responsible for maintaining the facility in a condition that meets state and federal permit requirements. Supervises and evaluates assigned staff; develops goals and expectations for operators, handles all employee concerns, directs work assignments, counsels and disciplines employees when necessary, and completes employee performance appraisals. Reviews the work of Operators for accuracy/completion and to ensure compliance with local, state and federal regulations. Communicates with employees to ensure proper plant operation of the Standard Operating Procedures. Prepares and maintaining reports, logs, and records on a daily, weekly, and monthly basis. Controls treatment plant processes, chemical dosages, and equipment used to purify, treat and clarify water for human consumption and for industrial and commercial use. Operates and controls various pumps and valves to regulate the flow of water through the treatment plant and distribution system. Assists in performing a variety of laboratory tests to determine the chemical composition of water and to ensure compliance with federal and state regulations for turbidity, chlorine, fluoride, pH, iron and manganese; makes adjustments to chemical dosages as necessary. Records plant operation data from observations, instrumentation and laboratory tests; records test results for reporting to state agency as appropriate. Receives and/or prepares letters, reports, correspondence, forms and other documentation; reviews, processes, and/or forwards as appropriate; maintains files and logs; performs other clerical duties.

Decision Making

Selects from multiple procedures and methods to accomplish tasks. Applies organizational policies. Leadership Provided Has formal supervisory authority over work group (typically at least 4-5 employees) to include discipline, performance management, scheduling, training, etc.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

This is a partial listing of necessary knowledge, skills, and abilities required to perform the job successfully. It is not an exhaustive list.

Knowledge of the operation, methods and procedures of a wastewater treatment plant; knowledge of the machinery used for wastewater treatment and pumping stations; knowledge of mechanical equipment; knowledge of basic machinery preventive maintenance and repair; knowledge of State and Federal rules governing wastewater discharges and worker's safety; knowledge of laboratory procedures and terminology; knowledge of Chemistry terminology; knowledge of microorganisms; knowledge of Back Flow Prevention. Skill in communicating effectively verbally and in writing; skill in solving complex problems independently; skill in operating incinerators, composite samplers, and various lab test equipment; skill in operating a computer and computer software; skill in performing analysis of laboratory data; Skill in basic math and chemistry, in oral and written communication, and in supervision; skill in water plant operation and in the use of maintenance equipment and water analysis equipment; skill in utilizing various software programs relevant to the position; skill in organizational, management, human resources techniques. Ability to use independent judgment and discretion in managing subordinates including the handling of emergency situations, determining and deciding upon procedures to be implemented, setting priorities, maintaining standards, and resolving problems; ability to comprehend, interpret, and apply regulations, procedures, and related information; ability to handle required mathematical calculations; ability to treat water in a safe, effective manner; ability to work outdoors in any kind of weather; ability to read and understand design drawings and plans; ability to operate a vehicle; ability to diagnose and correct equipment malfunctions.

Minimum Qualifications

High school diploma or General Equivalency Diploma (GED). 5 years' of work experience in a wastewater plant or a related area.

Preferred Education & Experience

High school diploma or General Equivalency Diploma (GED) and 5 years' of work experience in a wastewater plant, including 2 years' of supervisory experience in a wastewater plant or related area. Licensures and Certifications Valid State of Georgia Drivers License required. Class I Water Distribution License required. Forklift Certification desirable.

jobs.description:
This is where
your work makes a difference.

At Baxter, we believe every person—regardless of who they are or where they are from—deserves a chance to live a healthy life. It was our founding belief in 1931 and continues to be our guiding principle. We are redefining healthcare delivery to make a greater impact today, tomorrow, and beyond.

Our Baxter colleagues are united by our Mission to Save and Sustain Lives. Together, our community is driven by a culture of courage, trust, and collaboration. Every individual is empowered to take ownership and make a meaningful impact. We strive for efficient and effective operations, and we hold each other accountable for delivering exceptional results.

Here, you will find more than just a job—you will find purpose and pride.

Your Role at Baxter

As the Remediation Lead, you will provide senior Quality leadership for the design, integration, and execution of complex remediation programs at Round Lake Drug Delivery. You will translate regulatory observations, inspection findings, quality-system gaps, and internal commitments into practical, risk-based plans that deliver sustainable compliance, protect product quality, and support patient safety.

You will serve as the single point of integration across remediation workstreams, establishing disciplined governance, clarifying accountability, managing interdependencies, and providing transparent, fact-based reporting to site and enterprise leadership. You will partner closely with Quality, Manufacturing, Engineering, Laboratories, Supply Chain, Regulatory Affairs, IT, and other functions while preserving the technical accountability of process owners and subject-matter experts.

This role is ideal for an experienced Quality leader who combines deep pharmaceutical compliance knowledge with strong program leadership, sound regulatory judgment, and a demonstrated ability to drive complex work to evidence-based and sustainable closure.

What You'll Be Doing

Lead the development, integration, and execution of site remediation strategies arising from regulatory inspections, Warning Letters, OAI classifications, health-authority commitments, audits, quality-system assessments, and significant recurring quality signals.
Translate commitments and identified gaps into clearly defined workstreams, accountable owners, milestones, dependencies, deliverables, interim controls, effectiveness measures, and objective closure evidence.
Establish and maintain a risk-based remediation master plan and governance cadence that provides clear visibility to progress, overdue actions, critical-path constraints, resource needs, decision requirements, and emerging risks.
Provide independent Quality oversight and constructive challenge to ensure remediation plans are technically sound, scientifically justified, regulatorily defensible, feasible, and aligned with commitments made to health authorities and internal governance bodies.
Drive cross-functional execution across Quality, Manufacturing, Engineering, Maintenance, Facilities, Laboratories, Supply Chain, Regulatory Affairs, IT, Training, and Operational Excellence to remove barriers and maintain alignment.
Strengthen investigations, root-cause analysis, CAPA design, change control, quality risk management, data integrity, and effectiveness verification to prevent recurrence and improve Quality System performance.
Provide leadership and oversight for remediation involving sterile pharmaceutical manufacturing, aseptic processing, terminal sterilization, sterility assurance, contamination control, particulate and microbiological risk management, process validation, and equipment qualification.
Coordinate the preparation and Quality review of regulatory responses, remediation status reports, inspection-readiness materials, leadership presentations, and supporting evidence packages.
Ensure remediation records are complete, traceable, internally consistent, inspection-ready, and readily retrievable, with a clear linkage between identified gaps, corrective actions, implementation evidence, and effectiveness outcomes.
Identify systemic themes, recurring failure modes, cross-workstream dependencies, and opportunities to simplify or standardize controls without weakening compliance requirements.
Partner with functional leaders to assess resource and capability needs, sequence priorities, manage scope and change, and escalate decisions that could affect regulatory commitments, product quality, patient safety, or remediation outcomes.
Create and monitor leading and lagging indicators such as milestone adherence, overdue-action aging, first-pass deliverable acceptance, CAPA effectiveness, recurrence, and evidence-readiness to verify that improvements are implemented and sustained.
Coach workstream leads and subject-matter experts on clear problem definition, measurable deliverables, disciplined execution, evidence-based closure, and concise executive and regulatory communication.
Serve as a trusted advisor to site and enterprise leadership, providing direct, objective assessments of progress, uncertainty, residual risk, and areas requiring intervention.

What You'll Bring

Bachelor's degree in Pharmacy, Chemistry, Microbiology, Engineering, Life Sciences, Quality, or a related technical discipline.
At least 8 years of progressively responsible experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, or another highly regulated manufacturing environment, including significant experience in Quality, Compliance, or Regulatory functions.
Demonstrated leadership of complex, cross-functional remediation, compliance, Quality System, or transformation programs involving multiple workstreams and senior stakeholders.
Experience supporting FDA or other global health-authority inspections, regulatory responses, and remediation associated with regulatory observations, Warning Letters, OAI classifications, Consent Decrees, or comparable enforcement actions.
Strong knowledge of cGMPs, pharmaceutical Quality Systems, investigations, CAPA, change control, quality risk management, data integrity, validation, and inspection readiness.
Experience in sterile pharmaceutical manufacturing, including aseptic processing, sterility assurance, contamination control, injectable products, IV solutions, and/or terminal sterilization.
Ability to critically evaluate technical and procedural content, distinguish completed activity from demonstrated effectiveness, and identify weak assumptions, insufficient controls, or unsupported closure evidence.
Proven ability to influence without direct authority, make sound risk-based decisions, manage ambiguity, and drive accountability and follow-through across functions.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex technical information into clear, decision-oriented executive and regulatory updates.
Strong program and portfolio management discipline, including management of scope, milestones, dependencies, risks, issues, decisions, resources, and change.
Ability to work effectively in a 24/7 regulated manufacturing environment and provide support outside standard business hours when significant quality, inspection, or remediation needs arise.
Ability to travel as needed to support regulatory inspections, remediation activities, and enterprise governance.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in a scientific, engineering, quality, regulatory, or business discipline.
Formal certification in project or program management, Lean Six Sigma, quality management, or change management.
Experience leading remediation in a multi-building pharmaceutical operation or a complex sterile-manufacturing network.
Experience with electronic Quality Management Systems, remediation portfolio dashboards, evidence repositories, and executive governance forums.
Experience building organizational capability through coaching, leader standard work, structured problem solving, and disciplined performance management.

At Baxter, we believe every person—regardless of who they are or where they are from—deserves a chance to live a healthy life. It was our founding belief in 1931 and continues to be our guiding principle. We are redefining healthcare delivery to make a greater impact today, tomorrow, and beyond.

Here, you will find more than just a job—you will find purpose and pride.

Your Role at Baxter

As the Remediation Lead, you will provide senior Quality leadership for the design, integration, and execution of complex remediation programs at Round Lake Drug Delivery. You will translate regulatory observations, inspection findings, quality-system gaps, and internal commitments into practical, risk-based plans that deliver sustainable compliance, protect product quality, and support patient safety.

You will serve as the single point of integration across remediation workstreams, establishing disciplined governance, clarifying accountability, managing interdependencies, and providing transparent, fact-based reporting to site and enterprise leadership. You will partner closely with Quality, Manufacturing, Engineering, Laboratories, Supply Chain, Regulatory Affairs, IT, and other functions while preserving the technical accountability of process owners and subject-matter experts.

This role is ideal for an experienced Quality leader who combines deep pharmaceutical compliance knowledge with strong program leadership, sound regulatory judgment, and a demonstrated ability to drive complex work to evidence-based and sustainable closure.

What You'll Be Doing

Lead the development, integration, and execution of site remediation strategies arising from regulatory inspections, Warning Letters, OAI classifications, health-authority commitments, audits, quality-system assessments, and significant recurring quality signals.
Translate commitments and identified gaps into clearly defined workstreams, accountable owners, milestones, dependencies, deliverables, interim controls, effectiveness measures, and objective closure evidence.
Establish and maintain a risk-based remediation master plan and governance cadence that provides clear visibility to progress, overdue actions, critical-path constraints, resource needs, decision requirements, and emerging risks.
Provide independent Quality oversight and constructive challenge to ensure remediation plans are technically sound, scientifically justified, regulatorily defensible, feasible, and aligned with commitments made to health authorities and internal governance bodies.
Drive cross-functional execution across Quality, Manufacturing, Engineering, Maintenance, Facilities, Laboratories, Supply Chain, Regulatory Affairs, IT, Training, and Operational Excellence to remove barriers and maintain alignment.
Strengthen investigations, root-cause analysis, CAPA design, change control, quality risk management, data integrity, and effectiveness verification to prevent recurrence and improve Quality System performance.
Provide leadership and oversight for remediation involving sterile pharmaceutical manufacturing, aseptic processing, terminal sterilization, sterility assurance, contamination control, particulate and microbiological risk management, process validation, and equipment qualification.
Coordinate the preparation and Quality review of regulatory responses, remediation status reports, inspection-readiness materials, leadership presentations, and supporting evidence packages.
Ensure remediation records are complete, traceable, internally consistent, inspection-ready, and readily retrievable, with a clear linkage between identified gaps, corrective actions, implementation evidence, and effectiveness outcomes.
Identify systemic themes, recurring failure modes, cross-workstream dependencies, and opportunities to simplify or standardize controls without weakening compliance requirements.
Partner with functional leaders to assess resource and capability needs, sequence priorities, manage scope and change, and escalate decisions that could affect regulatory commitments, product quality, patient safety, or remediation outcomes.
Create and monitor leading and lagging indicators such as milestone adherence, overdue-action aging, first-pass deliverable acceptance, CAPA effectiveness, recurrence, and evidence-readiness to verify that improvements are implemented and sustained.
Coach workstream leads and subject-matter experts on clear problem definition, measurable deliverables, disciplined execution, evidence-based closure, and concise executive and regulatory communication.
Serve as a trusted advisor to site and enterprise leadership, providing direct, objective assessments of progress, uncertainty, residual risk, and areas requiring intervention.

What You'll Bring

Bachelor's degree in Pharmacy, Chemistry, Microbiology, Engineering, Life Sciences, Quality, or a related technical discipline.

Job Overview

APTIM is seeking a Project Environmental Data Analyst
that will work exclusively on a Key Client National Account to manage client and vendor data sets presented in various formats and turn them into reliable datasets, project databases, and useful Power BI Dashboards. The Environmental Data Analyst will work with project managers and technical specialists to understand reporting needs, recommend meaningful metrics and trend analyses, evaluate data workflows, and independently build and maintain tools from initial requirements through ongoing use. The successful candidate will have advanced Microsoft Excel and Power BI skills, sound analytical judgment, and the ability to deliver accurate, understandable information that supports client reporting and project decisions. Environmental data and AI experience are valued but are not required.

Key Responsibilities/Accountabilities

Partner with project managers and technical specialists to define reporting objectives, identify relevant metrics and trends, and translate project questions into practical data tools and dashboards.
Demonstrate expertise in data management, automation, and interactive business intelligence to transform multiple streams of raw data into automated reporting formats.
Combine, clean, standardize, and reconcile data across multiple Microsoft Excel workbooks, client data exports, vendor reports, and project databases; resolve inconsistent identifiers, formats, dates, units, duplicate records, and missing information.
Analyze datasets across sites, reporting periods, and data sources to identify trends, discrepancies, exceptions, and opportunities for improvement; explain findings and data limitations to the project team.
Design, build, and maintain Power BI reports and dashboards, including Power Query transformations, data models, relationships, DAX measures, filters, and clear visualizations tailored to client needs.
Evaluate existing data collection and reporting workflows; develop repeatable Excel and Power Query processes that reduce manual work and improve consistency and timeliness.
Build and maintain project databases and structured datasets, including tables, unique identifiers, relationships, validation rules, and data dictionaries that support reliable analysis and reporting.
Validate calculations and dashboard results against source records; document reconciliation checks, assumptions, and unresolved exceptions, and coordinate technical interpretation with environmental specialists.
Own ongoing tool maintenance, including data refreshes, troubleshooting, updates, and change testing to ensure accuracy.
Manage assigned data deliverables across the program’s datasets, estimate effort, meet agreed schedules, and communicate priorities and issues with limited day-to-day supervision.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in data analytics, information systems, computer science, or a related field.
Minimum of 5 years of experience in data analysis, data management, and support of tools used by project teams or clients.
Advanced Microsoft Excel proficiency, including complex formulas, lookup functions, PivotTables, data validation, Power Query, and combining and reconciling data across workbooks.
Demonstrated Power BI development experience including data preparation, relational modeling, DAX calculations, report design, publishing, and maintaining refresh processes in Power BI Service.
Ability to translate loosely defined reporting needs into working solutions, organize concurrent assignments, document methods, and explain results clearly to nontechnical users.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with environmental or EHS data, such as hazardous waste, stormwater, inspection findings, compliance tracking, or sustainability metrics; experience supporting consulting or client project delivery.
SQL querying skills and experience with database platforms or environmental data management systems.
Experience with Power Automate, VBA, Python, or similar tools to automate data preparation and reporting.
Project management experience, including coordinating with cross-functional teams, managing schedules and deliverables, communicating risks and priorities, and supporting account managers to deliver successful client project execution.
Experience applying AI tools to data extraction, reconciliation, analysis, or workflow automation, with validation of outputs and appropriate protection of client information.
